utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. You've got the standard three quarters of an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your statement, you say that your family has been living for hundreds of years in the village of Racak. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that there were families of Serb ethnicity in Racak?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the Serbs live in Racak?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked when, because --

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, for as long as I remember. They have now left Recak. They started leaving even before. Only one was left behind, as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, all right. Your compatriot Drita Emini told us that there were no Serb families in Racak.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the middle of Petrova, Prishtina, Recak, on the way to these places, there were about three households before, and until the massacre at Recak, they still lived there. There was only one single person living there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that relations with the Serbs were never good. That's what you say in your statement, and there were only three families there in those parts.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Shtime, there were -- relations were good until 1999. Nobody harassed the Serbs, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did they begin harassing the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That presupposes that there was any harassment. Now, Mr. Beqiri, the question should be in this form: Were the Serbs subject to any harassment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody harassed the Serbs. It was the other way around: The Serbs harassed the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, you have clipped my cross-examination. I don't see why you should be asking questions instead of me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, listen. If you ask questions which contain a presupposition which is unfair to the witness, you will be stopped. The question should have been as I put it: Were the Serbs harassed? Or if you want to put it this way: The Serbs were harassed, weren't they? Either way. But you can't ask a question which presupposes an answer which the witness hasn't given. If you do that, you will be stopped.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I hope that that criterion will be applied by you to the opposite side too, that asks only questions of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me. You said you were a taxi driver and so on. I can see here for four years, you say. Now, where were you registered, as you were a taxi driver in Racak? Where did you pay your taxes? Where did you pay your electricity bills and other dues and the basic things that citizens have to pay?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked as a taxi driver from 1992 to 1994 in the Shtime municipality. That is where I paid my taxes until 1994. In 1994, I gave up work as I could not go on working there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that from 1992 to 1996 you worked that way. Now you say 1994. Were you in fact working for two or for four years?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked for two years. The rest of the period I gave up because I was not feeling very well, although I continued paying taxes until 1996. The police forced me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you were an inhabitant of Racak and you were a taxi driver and you moved around, I'm sure you were well aware of the situation in the municipality of Stimlje and in the whole of Racak, in fact. You knew what was going on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I haven't had those powers or their powers, rather. I looked after my family, and you should know these things better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me this: When for the first time in an organised way did the members of the KLA establish themselves in your region?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know anything on this. I don't know of any area in my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know at all how many members of the KLA there were in your parts immediately prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an exact figure. I could go and ask the military chiefs and superiors on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me roughly? I assume you would know roughly.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry to say I was not a member of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you whether you were a member. All I'm asking you is how many would you say there were in the region? A rough estimate. If you can't answer, just say, "I don't know," and we can move on.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. I was not a military superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you know who Mehmet Mustafa is from Racak?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many Mustafas. I do not know. I do not know this person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mehmet Mustafa. Do you have many Mehmet Mustafas in Racak?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many Mehmet Mustafas. There are 300 households in the village, over 2.000 inhabitants, and I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm thinking about the Mehmet Mustafa whose house was the headquarters of the KLA in Racak. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who Buja Shukri is?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is he, then?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this person after the war. He is from Bujan. If he's the one that you want, you can call him to appear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know who dug trenches around Racak? Did you take part in that trench digging?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not take any part. I know I wasn't personally involved. It was the army that did that. And your army was stationed in Recak intermittently or almost all the time after the massacre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about trenches, the trenches that they dug for the KLA, that the KLA dug and civilians from Racak who assisted the KLA. I'm asking you about what other witnesses from Racak have already said. Do you know anything about those trenches yourself?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say on what they did and what they dug. All I know is that the army dug those trenches at Pisha, the army station, the tanks, the police, and all the forces were stationed there. That is all I know. And I know what happened to Recak on 15th of January. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the KLA and the inhabitants of Racak did not dig trenches and there were none of their trenches in Racak or its environs; is that right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Recak itself, there weren't any. On the hills overlooking it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't see anything of that?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't go out because my house was a target from Ceska, and heavy artillery had it within range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you didn't see anything, any of those trenches or anything else or any KLA activity or any members of the KLA. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in your statement, you say: "The Serbs wanted --" and I'm quoting this from your statement, what you said: "The Serbs wanted to expel all the Albanians from Kosovo, and they wanted to bring in people of their own ethnicity from Bosnia, Croatia, and to have them take up residence on our land." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness finish. Yes. Go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of them were there. The Serbs of Shtime lived in Recak, and they stayed there until the massacre on January 15th. This happened at a quarter to seven. My brother was killed from a distance of 50 metres. Then they shot at me. It caught my hat. Then they -- they shot one -- my cousins Zenir and Halim of 12 years of age.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I don't think that this has anything to do with the question I asked him. So would you please bear that in mind, especially in view of the fact that my time is limited and not to be wasted on answers to questions I did not ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. You put the passage about the Serbs wanting to expel all the Albanians. That's an example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: As you said --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is to say, I said that he claimed and he confirmed that the Serbs wanted to bring in their own people from Bosnia, Croatia, et cetera, but he's not giving an example of that, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please: Did the Serbs from Bosnia and Croatia ever try and ever -- try to settle or come to Racak? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they came to Recak, on the hills overlooking Recak, and they were there at the time of the massacre and stayed on for about three months, after the massacre, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you talking about the army and the police?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Serbian police and the army, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the Serbs from Bosnia and Croatia that you said wanted to settle on your land. Did anybody actually come to settle in Racak?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Serbs were all mixed up. They were all mixed up with your Serbs, rather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, please, who told you that the Serbs wanted to expel the Albanians? Who told you that? Who did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Recak was burned down in 1998, in August, that is, August the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you that, that the Serbs wanted to expel the Albanians? That was my question. Who did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was obvious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't understand. Did somebody come to your house to expel you from your house and tell you to get out and leave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has taken the matter as far as he can. Just a moment, Mr. Beqiri. It's no point arguing about this. It's one of the issues we're going to have to decide. He's given an example, as I've said. Now, let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I bothering you here, Mr. May, with my questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Just move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean generally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that on the 15th of January, at 6.45, you heard a loud explosion, a big blast, and then you go on to say that you took to the hill straight away. Why did you decide to climb up the hill?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On January the 15th, 1999, at 6.45, we heard shots and went out into the yard. My brother was coming from his own house to come over to us upon hearing these shots. And then we proceeded uphill, through the valley - Beqaviq, it's called - to go to the mountains in order to save the family. Other villagers joined up with us, and we went to Cesta, and that's where Serbian police and army had encircled the entire village of Recak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The question was: Why did you decide to climb up the hill? And your answer is: To save the family. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many of you were there when you set out, when you set out to climb the hill? How many of you?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sixteen from my own family. There were about 12 households in my neighbourhood alone, and all of them went out in order to save their lives from the police forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So that would make it 150 of you. If we count 16 from your own family and perhaps a little fewer from other households, that would make it 150 people, roughly; right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't count them, because bullets from Serbian forces were showering on us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you say 13 [sic] households, and your family with 16 family members. If the other households numbered only ten members, that would make it 200. So you say -- or 150. So you say you all left, did you, all that many people?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all left. I just could not count them. There were also refugees from Belinca, five or six of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So in that whole group, was anybody armed? This group of yours that took to the hills, were you armed?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all civilians. Children of 12 years of age, they could not have been soldiers, and they were killed there, the names of them Beqiri.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the 12-year-old children. What I'm asking you is whether it is correct that you moved towards the trenches which you had already dug out and that represented the fire power and positions of the KLA when the shooting started. So this is a direct question. I'm not asking you about the children who were 12 years old.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness knows nothing about the trenches, so to allege that he had already dug them out is a misrepresentation of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that he had dug them out, in person. I don't know what the translation was like. I'm looking at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The question, Mr. Beqiri, for you is: Were any of your group who went up the mountain armed?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and I didn't get an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, none of us was armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. A moment ago you said that there were some children who were 12 years old who were victims. I don't know that any children died who were 12 years old.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You do not apparently have knowledge of anything. If you had been in full knowledge, you would have known that people were killed. And Sahide was killed, and the body was removed and the grave remained empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a new fact now, that some children were killed in Racak as well; right? So far we haven't had this fact brought forward. We haven't been made aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You killed children, the elderly, civilians, everybody who was there, unarmed. And we couldn't have stayed in the village had we been armed. The Serbs wouldn't have allowed us. We were all farmers. All of us were unarmed. The Serbs did all they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you explain how Riza Beqiri was killed, Zenel Beqiri, Halim Beqiri. Now, who shot at these people? Who fired at them?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbian forces, yours. And they were all Serbs from Shtime, policemen from Shtime. They were put in uniforms as paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please. You said that you saw their suffering, how they were killed. Did you actually see that? Try to remember your very own description of that. You speak of how they were killed.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were killed from a distance of 50 metres by your forces, and also the shells that you fired from Cesta, Pishat, Geshtenjet, from every side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Does that mean that they were killed by shells?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were killed by bullets, not by shells, and then they were mutilated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not understand you well. Please. First they were killed by bullets and then by shells, or first by shells and then by bullets, and then they were massacred; is that how you put it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has responded. You asked him whether they were killed by bullets or shells, and the answer was: "They were killed by bullets, not by shells."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I don't know what your objection is in relation to my question. I'm asking him about the order that he presented a minute ago, and I really do not see why you are intervening, because I simply do not understand what he had said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Because your questions are confused and liable to confuse the witness. It's not fair to him. Now, what is the point you want to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, what killed these people, the people whose killing you have described?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are your comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Would you just -- Mr. Beqiri, I know it is repeating the evidence, but we'll get there more quickly. You were asked about the Beqiris who were killed, the members of the family. Now, what killed them? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were killed by Serbian forces, by barbarians --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- at a distance of 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What? What? What was it that killed them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bullets from machine-guns and from sniper guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it wasn't shells that killed them; right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not here. You fired the shells above Recak to clear the area so that the KLA wouldn't come to Recak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now you explained what the purpose of the shells was. Could you please explain the third element to me now? You said that they were massacred after they were killed. How is it that they were massacred or mutilated?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After they gathered people, they put them in the houses and then they beat them. And I couldn't see them because I was in a different place. And then there were wounded, and then observers came. And then when I came down, they said that they were coming from Bebush Hill, about ten metres distance. And then they fired on Hysni and Haziri. And then some villagers went with me, and there were other villagers there, and then we took shelter in a kind of cellar. And there they shot at us with sniper guns from Bebush Hill. And we were staying in this cellar. Earlier, we heard a kind of shouting, and there they had killed my cousin Bajram Mehmeti and Hanemshah, his daughter, and his son was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The question was: How is it that the bodies were mutilated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One, they took off the head. They gouged out the eyes. I saw this in the mosque. When they took them to the mosque on the 16th, I was there, and it was the most barbaric thing that I had ever seen. Chetniks did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say that they shot at them with sniper rifles from the hills, and you say that they shot at them from a 50-metre distance. Are both correct or is one correct or the other?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't far from the hill. It was only about 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. You say that they were firing shells from the hills so the KLA could not get close to you. How far away was the police from you and how far away was the KLA? You were at the spot where you were. So how far away were the police from you and how far away was the KLA?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, please, because I don't understand the question. The KLA was four kilometres away, in Rance. It was in Petrova and also in Mullopolc to the south. But I didn't see them because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that moment, could you see a single policeman shooting at you?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they entered and got us out of the houses, out of Hysni Emini's house, there was a policeman came in, and they took out some members of my family first and killed a brother on the doorstep, and then a policeman from Shtime came. And I don't know his name, but I know that his father's name was Branko. And he said, "Go outside." And I went out first, first of the members of the family who were there. And then when I went out to the door, they were putting on masks. There was Bozo; Milos, son of Pero; Marinkovic, and Fetke from Shterpc, and the others. But when I saw my cousin had fallen, and then they put the automatic rifle at my throat, I wasn't able any more to see anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, a short while ago you mentioned that observers came in. When is it -- when did you first see the observers on the 15th of January? What time was it then?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The observers came at 5.00 or 6.00 in the evening, when they had come to take the wounded. And Zuhra, Feta, and Hasan Maliqi, and there's Bajram's small son Elhami, and a woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them that morning up on the hill? Because they have those characteristic orange vehicles. Did you see them standing up there on the hill?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see them because I was under a kind of blockade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say in your statement that you were already in the hills, 100 metres into the hills and that you saw policemen on the road. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are comments. This is not quite correct. I said that when I went out of my house, ten metres away you could see Cesta Hill from my house. I saw tanks up there from where they fired. And my brother, cousin that were killed, and my neighbour's wife, I saw from this place where I was. I saw the tanks on Cesta. These are comments that you're making.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you saw observers, that is to say that observers came around 5.00 or 6.00 that evening. Why, since at that time our police was not there, at that particular time, why did you not indicate to the observers the other persons that were killed and that you mention? Why did you not tell the observers about them?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The observers asked us about the people who were killed, and the wounded were taken for hospital, and the people who were massacred on Bebush Hill, 24 were killed, five survived. And the others were found on the 16th, were found on that hill. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you did tell the observers that on that day.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 15th, in the afternoon, you informed them about that, about these people who had been killed and about everything that had happened; is that right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent. Tell me, now, who told you to carry the bodies on the 17th, in the morning, to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The verifiers came on the 16th and looked round. And at 12.00, they came with helicopter, came to the mutilated, the massacred people, and then went back. And in the evening, the villagers took them to the mosque before burial. And I went on the 16th -- on the 17th - and this was Sunday - and I helped carry them. And we carried them to the mosque, six of us. People who were killed in the Berisha neighbourhood up above. And then you came again, and you wanted to come enter and take them. And there was fighting on the 17th and on the 18th. You took the dead to the hospital in Prishtina with strong police and military forces and kept them for a month in the hospital and then sent them back. Twenty-six brought back. These were the bodies. And we buried them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, tell me, did you see William Walker on the 16th in Racak?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came and saw the victims, members of the Beqiri family, and went to Bebush Hill. I couldn't leave my home at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time did he come to the village?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look at my watch. Whether it was 10.00 or 11.00 or 12.00, I don't know, but he came between about 10.00 and 12.00 on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you say that you saw Mehmet Jakupi's body decaying when you saw the other bodies. How come his body was already in a state of decay and the others weren't?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all decaying, but I had -- he was a friend of mine. And when I saw him, I was very upset at what they had done to him, because there were people with their heads removed, eyes gouged out, hearts taken out, and only barbarians, Chetniks could do that. Albanians could never do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw hearts plucked out, heads cut off, and what other acts of barbarism did you see, the ones that you've been referring to?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What more terrible things can I say? What more terrible things are there than mutilating people like that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, say everything that you saw. I'm interested in all that you mentioned: hearts plucked out, heads cut off. What else was it that you saw?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They put the women inside that day, and not a single of your policemen were killed on that day. The women and the children were all corralled in, and the men were wrested away from their families, from their women and children, taken away and killed over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you about what these mutilated bodies looked like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have dealt sufficiently with that. The witness has given his evidence and your time is now finished. Yes. No, you have had your time. Now, are there any questions from the amicus? Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I would have a few questions for Mr. Beqiri. Questioned by Mr. Tapuskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Beqiri, in your statement, you said that your brother, Riza Beqiri, had two sons in the KLA. Beqe was a member of the KLA from the very outset; is that right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Beqe was a member since August 1998, when Recak was burned. That was when he went to join the KLA. On the 2nd, after they killed his brother -- his father and two brothers, he too reached for a gun and went up to the hills, on the 20th of May, 1999 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you, Mr. Beqiri, about this son that you had mentioned who had been in the KLA from 1998. Where did he operate as a member of the KLA? Did he operate in the village where you were or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Rance. He was stationed there, in the village of Rance, while the second one was in the village of Petrova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you about this other one. At the moment when what happened, happened in Racak on the 15th, where was Beqe? In Rance? Is that where he was too?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Rance yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Rance is only a few kilometres away from Racak; right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's four kilometres, or three; three or four, as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Beqiri, you said that on the 15th of January, when you heard an explosion, a blast, that you went -- at 6.45, that you went out into the yard.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, from the yard, together with the others, you proceeded to go elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- my family -- go to another place, but my brother, with my daughter and his wife and that son who was killed, Halim, and Hasan, and we went up ten metres above the house. And they were killed in my neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Beqiri, I first wanted to ask you about the following: When you left the house so abruptly on the 15th of January, what did you wear? What kind of clothing did you wear?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The usual, like you see me here, civilian clothes. As I was there when I heard the shots, just got up, put the clothes on. My brother was on his way to call me out. We went out into the yard, and that is from where we saw that the entire village had been encircled. They probably entered the village from the direction of Belinca in the course of the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You wore one single suit; right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A jacket. Trousers, a jacket. What else could I put on?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. I'm interested in the following as well,

utterances.speaker: MR. BEQIRI
utterances.text: When you went uphill, you were actually ordered to go uphill; is that right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ordered us. They kept shooting at us every single day, in the direction of Recak, and it was the shots of these barbarians and Chetniks that made us go uphill. We knew that we couldn't stay indoors, because if they found somebody indoors, they mutilated them; they killed and mutilated them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Beqiri, in your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am referring to page 5 -- no. Page 4, the last paragraph in the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that Cvetko ordered you to go uphill. That's the way you put it when you gave this statement previously.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but Cvetkovic was not at my house, but at Hysni's house. That's where he came and forced us out. Cvetkovic, that is, came in and ordered us to go to the Bebush hill. We did not obey this order and instead headed in the opposite direction. The women went to Haxhi Musa's house, whilst we were told to go to the KLA. There weren't any other KLA there. There were only Serbian policemen from Shtime. Those were the ones who emerged and shot in our direction. Luckily, we survived. And then they descended down and came and took Sahide and took her away and went downhill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've understood that. I've understood that, Mr. Beqiri. But then you said here - and is that correct? - that you fled in all directions and hid wherever you could.

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to my cousin's, Mehdi's, after being shot at and surviving. So I went to my cousin's, and that is from where I observed what happened at Bebush Hill, where machine-guns were used. This happened at about 1.00 or 2.00 or 12.00, round about that time. That is when they were killed, and we could easily see it from where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me one more thing, please: On that day, on the 15th, was a single member of the KLA in the village killed? Did any one of them lose their lives?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was then in my neighbourhood [as interpreted]. I did not see any. Even if there were any -- I don't think there were. There were civilians. There were no KLA there. I haven't heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the next day? Did you hear about any KLA members being killed on the next day?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Always, always civilians, on the 16th, on the 17th. The only people I saw were civilians who were killed. There were no soldiers in Recak, no killed soldiers in Recak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question, Mr. Beqiri: Do you know how many Serb policemen lost their lives by the mosque on the 18th? Is it true that 17 were killed? Do you know anything about that, when they were taking over the bodies?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 17th, police were unable -- oh, I see. The 18th. I was at Lluzhak on the 12th, and I do not know what happened in the clashes between the Liberation Army and the Serbian barbarians. I don't know who was killed and how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have one brief area for clarification, if I may, arising out of cross-examination. Re-examined by Mr. Ryneveld:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I understood you correctly under cross-examination, you indicated that you saw the observers come into Racak at about 5.00 or 6.00 in the evening on the 15th of January. So far, have I got that right?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were then asked by the accused about whether you had told the observers about all the bodies that had been killed. Do you remember being asked about that?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Through the interpreters who were with the verifiers, we related the fact of the six that had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The six that had been killed. That's the point for clarification. Did you also indicate that there were 24 killed and five survivors on Bebush Hill that were discovered on the 16th? Is that what your evidence was?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All we heard was that these were taken by the Serbian police and gaoled. On the next day, however, they were found. I found five of them up in the hills, and his name was Rame, from the Gashis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I can stop you there. It's my fault. Let me simplify my question. At 5.00 or 6.00 at night on the 15th of January, did you know about anybody who had been killed up in Bebush Hill at that time? In other words, by 5.00 or 6.00 on the 15th, did you know about that yet?

utterances.speaker: XHEMAJL BEQIRI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know. I did not know. All I knew was that they had been taken away by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Beqiri, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next witness, can I ask something about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Who is the next witness, please, Ms. Romano?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The next witness is Nusret Shabani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I informed you two days ago that I was given a whole truckload of papers, and I asked you when you thought that I had time to read through all that. And this is what I got this morning. Have a look here at this whole pile of material. Yesterday, I received another 1.000 pages and 350 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we're not going to deal with that now. We have in mind that there will be a very great deal of material which is coming to you - you've mentioned it - and in due course, we will be considering the future conduct of the case as a result, but at the moment, we are not concerned with it. We need to get on with the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't finish my sentence, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: The point is that -- [Interpretation] The point is that nothing that has not been disclosed to me in my own language I consider not to have been disclosed. And the second point is answer this question, please: Where, when do you think I can find time to read the truckload of papers that I was disclosed yesterday and the day before? So I have made two points. My first point is that I would like to have the documents disclosed in my own language; and secondly, when do you think I ought to read all this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Those are matters which we'll be considering in due course. They have nothing to do with the evidence at the moment. Now, let's have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I pointed out in the summary, this witness is unable to read the declaration, so it will need to be read to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That can be done in the usual way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness stand. The declaration can be put on the ELMO or perhaps the interpreters can read it. Is that possible? If they've got a copy and the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Romano:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you give us your full name.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Nusret Shabani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you born, Mr. Shabani?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I am 62 years old. I was born on the 6th of June, 1940.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you born in Racak and do you live in Racak?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Shabani, on the 2nd of May, 1999, you provided the Office of the Prosecutor with a statement. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, I think I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on 6 February this year in Racak, do you remember attending a meeting in the presence of a presiding officer appointed by the Registrar of this Tribunal? And in that meeting, do you remember being provided with a copy of your statement in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, you had the statement read out to you. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had the opportunity to confirm that the statement was true and correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. Some parts were correct. Some were not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can go into the points that were not correct later.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: At this point, the Prosecution will submit the statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 209.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: The summary of the witness statement is the following: The witness is a Kosovar Albanian residing in Racak, who is married and has four sons, two of which are in the KLA. From the summer of 1998 onwards, the police and army were positioned on the surrounding hills. There had been three or four clashes between the Serb police and the KLA, and at least four attacks on the village by the Serb forces prior to the event on 15 January 1999. On 15 January 1999, the witness woke up to the sound of gunfire and explosions. He saw soldiers entering the village, and he and his family left their home and went to Sadik Osmani's house. The men hid in the basement while the women and children stayed on the first floor. At approximately 1.00 p.m., the police arrived at the house with dark blue camouflage uniform, firing at the house while they approached. The men were taken out of the basement and ordered to lie on the ground where the police beat them with heavy sticks and verbally abused them. All of the men were in civilian clothing. The men were ordered to walk up to the ravine and go to the UCK in the village of Rance. En route, he and four others left the line of men and hid in a ditch. A few minutes later, he heard men screaming and bursts of gunfire. The witness and others remained in the ditch until 5.00 p.m., when they saw the Serb forces withdraw. He saw that the other men had been killed. He saw the bodies, and he also saw the body of his own son, Bajrush Shabani. After about two weeks, the witness went to his daughter-in-law's in Urosevac. Whilst there, the Serb army came to the house and fired at it. They lined up -- they lined the occupants up there in the street -- in the street and demanded money and cigarettes from them. The witness had a gun put onto his head. The same soldiers came back to the house the following night and demanded money. The witness went to Macedonia on the 26th of April, 1999. The scenes referred to by this witness are in the Racak binder. That's Prosecution Exhibit 156, tab 7, and they are, namely, the photographs showing Sadik Osmani's house and barn to the route that the men took to the ravine; the photographs in the section marked crime location 5, scene 10; and the photographs in the section marked crime location 5, scene 11. Your Honours, I don't think we need to show all the photographs. I'll just make reference on that. My last question is to the witness. He mentioned something that was not correct in his statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want to clarify that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: You mean me? There was one I had in mind, not two. At the Cesta Hill, there was only one son of mine who was a KLA member, not two. That is all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 1 of your statement, you say that your sons Nijaz and Rame were KLA soldiers; right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I said one. I think the translator made a mistake. I only said one. And if I had been able to, I also would have joined if I had known what was in store for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understood that you now made corrections as to where he was, not whether he was a soldier or not. So what you're saying is that the second son was not a soldier; right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. Only one son was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The son who was 33 years old, is that the one who was a KLA member?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No. The smaller one, the one who was 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did he join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I don't know. I do not know when he joined the KLA. I was not there. I cannot know the date, the month, the time he joined up. But had I known what was in store, I'd have joined as well. I will tell the truth here. If it's not true, I won't say it. I'm an old man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for joining the KLA, did he ask your agreement as his father? Did he ask you to agree and let him join?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I didn't see him when he went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the group of KLA deployed, the group that your son was a member of?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: They stayed in Rance. Ten or 12 kilometres beyond the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Rance is ten or 12 kilometres away from Racak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. Something like that. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what arms did they have?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Weapons? They didn't really have any at all. They were of no use. Hunting rifles, old guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they wear any uniforms?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: They didn't have uniforms. In the beginning they didn't, and later they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that later?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know these dates. There's no way I can know these things. I wasn't involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say in your statement that your village was attacked by the Serbs at least four times in the course of 12 months, over a period of 12 months. Now, on those four occasions when the village was attacked, did the members of the -- were the members of the KLA in the village and was your son amongst them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: The village was attacked, not as this man says, four times, it was attacked every day. And how was it attacked? It was attacked by lightweight weapons and then fired at with heavy guns from all sides. You did the shooting. And there was always firing every day with small arms. There was no KLA there. I said the KLA was never around in Racak. The KLA was in Rance, in the mountains. In the village, there was the population. Children, women, old people, the sick, those were the kind of people in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were -- you were there and I wasn't, and that's why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: [In Serbian] Yes. You can go ahead, Comrade, ask me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, let us remember this is a court, Mr. Shabani. So please bear that in mind. Now, Mr. Milosevic, what's your next question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The hill on which you say there was a camp that was called Cesta, and you say the policemen had a camp there; right? And I'm quoting you now. You say that there were three or four clashes between the KLA and the Serbs there, and the KLA won every time. That's what you wrote. Now, my question is the following: These clashes between the KLA and the Serbs, as you call them, do they coincide with the fighting from the previous question, that is to say, when they attacked the village four times, and so on?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And who do you mean when you say "the Serbs"? Do you mean the police forces? Are you thinking of the police?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, policemen and soldiers, policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you say that the KLA won every time, what do you mean by "won," that they "won"? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, they won there, but -- but there was nothing to be won. The KLA were there as -- they just watched because they didn't have any -- there were no borders. There were no frontiers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was an observer? I heard you say something like that. The KLA, you mean?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I mean the KLA watched the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And tell me how the KLA won if they observed the situation? I'm not quite clear on that point. Does it mean that the KLA did not fight? It just stood by, watching, observing?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Apart from these things that happened, then they returned back to where they belonged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Now, would you be so kind as to explain to me this: You said that on the hill, Cesta, that there were three or four clashes between the KLA and the Serbs and that the KLA always won. And as you say you did not take part in that but you were an eyewitness, could you describe to me what the fighting looked like? What actually happened in those clashes? Can you describe them to me?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Nothing happened. There was some shooting. Nothing else happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody killed or wounded in those clashes, for instance?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about that fighting? Did the KLA do the fighting with those hunting rifles that you mentioned a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did they kill any of the policemen or soldiers while they had no -- they themselves had nobody who was wounded on your side, that is, but did they kill a policeman or soldier on the opposite side, our side, that is?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did the KLA members go after they won, after these victories?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: There weren't any victories at all. They withdrew to the mountains, to Rance. I don't know where they withdrew to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how do you say there were no victories now, when you said that the KLA always won? Why weren't there any victories now? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Nobody won, neither the Serbs nor the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in this fighting, in these clashes, did the same members of the KLA take part, or would they take turns?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: How should I know? There's no way I could know that. There's no way I could know which units deployed where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I understood that you were an eyewitness, so that's why I was asking you if you know. If you don't know, say so.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: [In Serbian] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is it true that the members of the KLA who took part in this fighting were, for the most part, from Racak and the surrounding parts? Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I do not know who was there. I do not know who was there, which part of the country was there too, and what he did or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you talk about the struggles at Preduci [phoen]. You said you were an eyewitness and said that the KLA always won. Then you say that nobody won and that they withdrew. Quite simply, I'm asking you whether they were generally people from Racak and the surrounding parts, these people who took part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He says he does not know. Let's move on. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I can't know this. I can't know where people came from. I was not there to check their identity papers, to ask people who they were, what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Shabani. Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now a question for which you don't need to study an ID card. How many people were in that KLA unit, the unit that held the hill, and who was in command of the unit?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: How would I know who the commander would be? I don't know. I wasn't there to watch how big that group was. There was a small group. I don't know who the commander was. Neither do I know, neither there's any way I could know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I understand that you don't know who the commander was, but do you know how big the group was?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: [In Serbian] I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, give us a rough estimate. You don't know exactly, but tell us roughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Stop putting the witness under pressure in this way. It's simply not fair, endless repetition. Yes. It's time for an adjournment, in any event. Before we do adjourn, there are one or two administrative matters I want to deal with. Mr. Nice, since you're here, you can assist, or rather, perhaps let me mention these matters to you. There is an application on your part, an oral one, for certification in relation to the summarising witness. It would be helpful to have something in writing on that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- as to what it is you want certified and why.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And if you could let us have that within seven days. The next matter is the issue relating to contempt, not the witness. There is an issue which has arisen. Again, it would be helpful if you could report, do a report to us, and make some submissions as to what action you apply for.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is the newspaper matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I couldn't remember if it was an open-court matter or not. Seven days. The final matter is the exhibit to Dr. Baccard's evidence. You remember you raised an issue on that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- part of it. I think it would be helpful to hear oral submissions on that, given the state of the evidence, and we'll hear from the amicus. It was the additional exhibit, you may remember, to Dr. Baccard's evidence and whether it should be admitted or not. Again, if we could have that in seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think -- I think I provided -- if you want it in writing, I'll do it, yes, in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could you do something briefly in writing?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It would be of assistance, to see the way that you put it. Well, I'm sorry. Having said that, we wanted oral submissions. If you want to put in a skeleton, do; otherwise we'll simply fix a time for oral submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. On the last point, I think I provided the Chamber, at the time we last discussed this, with reference to the transcript page numbers, and I can be ready to make submissions about that at any time when we perhaps run short of a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. That would be helpful. But we'll give the amicus some time to think about it. The final matter is the matter which the accused raised, which we will have to consider, which is the amount of material which has been served on him and how that is to be fitted into the case as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. It, of course, relates to the next sector of the case. But perhaps we can discuss that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, at an appropriate time, but the Prosecution might like to consider the position. Yes. We'll adjourn. Mr. Shabani, you are giving evidence, so don't speak to anybody about it until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. If you would be back, please, at half past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was this group supplied, this KLA group that you said had held the hill? Did you or any members of your family take food to them, bring them supplies?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about this. I don't know who sent them bread and groceries and things like that. I wasn't involved in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they slept?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: [In Serbian] They slept in Rance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Xhemajl Batiqi, an Albanian from your village?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the case of the 18th of November, 1998, when members of the KLA burned the house of an Albanian? That was the Xhemajl Batiqi. Are you aware of that? This was in November 1998.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that members of the KLA who were precisely those KLA members who were in your area attacked the police several times? For example, on the 10th of September, 1998, and then the 29th of October, 1998, and the 10th of January, 1999? That's when policemen were killed, namely Sinisa Mihajlovic, Nazmi Oluri?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We don't need their names. Mr. Shabani -- a moment, please. Just a moment, please. Just a moment, Mr. Shabani. Do you know anything about what the accused is asking you? If you know nothing about it, just say you don't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about this thing he's asking about -- these things he's asking about. There's no way I can know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Mr. Milosevic, there is a witness coming who can deal with these matters. It's fairly pointless asking these witnesses from the village about these matters when they say they don't know. Now, what else have you got to ask him beyond questions about the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I have things to ask him, Mr. May. I've just started examining this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Albanians that you mention on page 2 of your statement and that you claim stayed at Sadik Osmani's house, Sadik Osmani being a relative of yours, so these people who you know and who were staying at Sadik Osmani's house, were they members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were not?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: They were not. One of them was, but he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only one of them was?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: [In Serbian] Only one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you explain the fact that such a large group of men, 22 of them --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: In that group, as I explained -- go on. Say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Shabani, would you go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was thrown out of the village of Recak. Not just me, but the whole village. And I was in other villages. And we came back for the day of Bajram. And either on the 8th or the 9th - I don't remember when - your forces came in and threw us out of Sadik Osmani's house. We weren't in the house. We were in the stable. There were 29 of us. There were 29 of us, all elderly people, children, people like that. And they came, your forces, and came into the shed in among the cows. And then they threw us outside, hands behind our backs. They beat us. They kicked us. They took our identity cards from our pockets. They put us in the yard, and they hit us with sticks, and they -- "Go on. Go up the hill," they told us. And when we got up there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Racak is a big village. It has 230 households. Did all the inhabitants happen to be in the village on the 15th of January?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: There were some in the village. There were some that hadn't come. They would come to -- for the Bajram festival, to celebrate it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the 15th of January. That's what I'm talking about. Are we both talking about that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: That's right, the 15th. That's right. 15th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the assertions correct that all the inhabitants or practically all the inhabitants left Racak as far back as the summer of 1998 and that smoke was coming only out of two chimneys on the 15th of January? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: There were some that hadn't come back. They hadn't gone far. They had gone to the plain of Kosova. They had gone to Shtime. They -- and some had come back. In general, they had come back. I didn't have any kind of list that I could go out into the street and find out who had come back and who had not come back. I was in my own home with my wife and family to celebrate the Bajram festival. That was why we were there. We were not just sitting there, waiting to be killed and massacred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell me roughly, 2.300 inhabitants of Racak. That's the population of Racak; right? How many of them were in Racak on that day? Was half there or a third, more than a half, more than a third? How many, roughly?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: There weren't all that many. Some had come and some had not come. I can't tell how many came. I can't tell how many came back. I can only tell you -- I can only talk about my own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to what you know, how many inhabitants of Racak were in Racak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's answered that, so there's no point going over it again. He says he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's not a difficult question for an inhabitant of Racak to give us the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. May. All right, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know that the police surrounded Racak and its outskirts on the 15th of January in order to catch the terrorists who had killed Svetislav Przic, a policeman, before that, precisely there in your parts?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Police. These people -- don't tell me who was killed, because I don't know anything about this. I only know my own business, about being captured and beaten and my family being killed and mutilated. Who else was killed? I don't know. Please. I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This unit that your son was in, did it take part in that attack on policeman Przic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. We've been over this for several minutes, not to say longer. No. Mr. Shabani, don't bother to answer. Now, Mr. Milosevic, unless you've got something new to ask this witness apart from questions about the KLA, we're going to close this cross-examination. If you want to go on, you must go on with another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. You don't want me to ask him anything about the KLA. So then I'll ask him the following:

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, on the 15th of January, did you see the OSCE observers with those orange vehicles of theirs?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No. I didn't see them on that day at all. On the 15th, no. I didn't see anybody with that kind. I wasn't free on the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the fighting in Racak end on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: [In Serbian] I don't know. [In Albanian] About 5.00. I don't know. Sometime round about then. There's no way I can tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around 5.00, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then after that, after that, did you see the OSCE observers after the fighting had ended on that day? Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No. I was sleeping in the hills the whole livelong night, in the rain and the snow. It was the next day that I came back to my home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that on the 15th, you did not even return to Racak.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No way. Of course I didn't return to Racak. I didn't come. I went back to the hills having -- once I survived your forces, I stayed the whole night, the whole livelong night in the hills, in the rain and the snow, and came back on the 16th without anything to eat or drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. This event that you describe on the 15th when you hid with a few more people in a ditch and then when this group got killed, immediately then, just after that, you saw them. That's what it says here on page 5 of your statement. You said: "I saw corpses with many bullet wounds. Their throats had been slit and their eyes had been gouged out." That is what you said, because -- that is your claim, that they had been killed there. So when did this happen? If I understood you correctly, you were hiding and then you got out after the fighting subsided, the shooting subsided, and then you found these people with their throats slit and with their eyes gouged out, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: We were hiding in the hills. There were five of us. When they finished their work of the massacre, they went back down and went into the village. And in the village, they started singing. So we stayed a further two or three hours up there before going down. And when we saw there were no more police and soldiers, we went and we saw the bodies. Some had had their heart torn out. Some had had their eyes gouged out. And we went up again, leaving the bodies there. We went up into the hills and we slept in the hills, as I said before, in the snow and the rain during the night, and in the morning, we went back home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you described now was what you saw on the afternoon of the 15th; right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say in the same paragraph: "All the men I mentioned earlier and said were killed in Racak were lying on that road. That is all I can say. There's nothing more I can say"?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that according to all these findings of teams both from home and abroad, all others, nobody's heart had been plucked out, nobody eyes had been gouged out, nobody had been slaughtered with a knife, none of those who had been killed in Racak on the 15th of January?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I don't know who was there and who was studying these things. There were five of us. And when the fighting finished and they went down, we -- and then we went and we saw the things that I said. I don't know who else went to look at them. There's no way I can know. I didn't go there again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say that somebody's heart had been plucked out, somebody's eyes had been gouged out. What do you mean by "a few" or "some"? Are you referring to two, three, five men? How many are you referring to, actually?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Well, about four, four there were, because some bodies were lying down, one above the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I mean everything that you said to us, you saw it on how many bodies?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said: "About four."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you. There were three. But then I didn't look closely at what had been done to them. We saw them, one by one. And this is true what I say. These are the things I have seen and experienced. I'm not going to talk about things I haven't seen and experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend the funeral of the persons who were killed in Racak on the day when this funeral took place?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No, I wasn't, because I was ill, because from the injuries I sustained, beaten by your men. My limbs were injured. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know or have you heard of that event, that on the day of the funeral, the KLA arrested a number of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He wasn't there. There's no point in asking him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask him whether he knew any of these people who were arrested at the funeral. People know when people are arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Shabani, do you know any of the people who were arrested at the funeral?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you a little while before: I wasn't at the funeral. I was at my daughter, at Loskobare. My daughter and my wife were at the funeral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Have you got anything more you want to ask the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I've switched off your microphone. You've got ten minutes more. Now, is there anything else you want to ask him on a different topic other than those which you've repeated?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I had just opened my mouth and I wanted to put a question to him, and I was not allowed to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 13th of February, 1999, almost a month later, did you hear about the kidnapping of Zeqiri Taip and Sherimi Jene [phoen], Albanians from your village, from Racak? Are you aware of this kidnapping that was done by the KLA, these fellow villagers of yours?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know about any crime that was committed in Racak or in the surrounding area? Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: There were no crimes committed in Recak. I'm not interested in the vicinity of Recak. I told you before: Places outside Recak or in the area, things that happened there, I don't know then, but I don't know of any crime that was committed in Recak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
