utterances.text: So you didn't see them on the 15th. You already told me that. When did you first see the OSCE verifiers in the area of your village?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: I didn't see the observers. I said before -- maybe I wrote that I said them [as interpreted], but I forgot. I didn't see any observers on that day anywhere. Because on that day - it was Friday - on the 16th, they took the bodies and put them in the mosque. Maybe I did meet an observer on that day. It is possible. But we went in to see the bodies, and they told us to hurry up because the Serbs were going to take the bodies. This is your army and the police. And then I went away to Koshare and Loskobare and to Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to anybody else except your own fellow villagers?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No. I don't know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Questioned by Mr. Tapuskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Shabani, I would have a few questions for you. I'm only interested in what happened on the 15th of January. In this statement of yours, it says that you stated that you heard three or four explosions and you saw the infantry coming. Is that right? Is that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Where were those explosions?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. You were at home at 7.00 in the morning and you heard this happening. You heard it while you were at home.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's true. There was no heavy artillery, only small-arms firing. No heavy artillery. There were no heavy artillery shells towards the village, inside the village. On the mountains and the hills, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've explained that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you said you escaped from the house and you went to your relatives' house. And now my question is the following: When you left home, what did you wear? What kind of clothes did you wear?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: The uniforms of the police, the army. I didn't cast my eyes on them. The uniforms that the army wore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't understand me.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: About me? The clothes that I've got on, this kind of clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't understand me, Mr. Shabani. What did you wear when you left home? What kind of clothes?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: The same clothes that you see me wearing here, the same kind of clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a number of questions in relation to what he says on page 4 of his statement, the English version, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Shabani, you described what happened in the yard of the house that you were in, and then you said here that the following happened: "Then they ordered us to get up and put our hands behind our heads." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you had your hands behind your head, they made you walk towards Bebush Hill; right? And all that time you were accompanied by a policeman?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No, no. We went on our own. Policemen did not come with us. We were on our own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Shabani, but you say here: "I saw a policeman in a dark blue camouflage uniform waving at the men to hurry up. He was about 20 metres away. We were walking slowly, in a line, with our hands behind our neck." So that means that you were walking that way all the time while the policeman was with you; right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you managed to escape to this ditch?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you heard a burst of gunfire, but you didn't see anything; right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At 5.00 in the afternoon, in that same -- you left that same ditch, and you say: "With me in the ditch were Imer Hakipi, Ali Qazimi, Avdi Bilalli, and Rame Shabani."

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Avdi Bilalli with you throughout that time in the ditch, and was he conscious? While he was in the ditch with you, was he fully conscious, like you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes. He was at a distance. He was not with the group. We were on higher ground. It was our destiny to survive the attack, because we could have been killed as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say here that Avdi Bilalli was with you the whole time. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: [In Serbian] Yes, he was. [In Albanian] Yes. We went uphill, up the mountain, spent the night there and returned the next day together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him next to you all the time? He was three or four metres away.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: We were together. He was at a distance of about five metres away. We were lying down, prone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he unconscious?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: [In Serbian] I don't know that. [In Albanian] I don't know about that. He knows these things. He can come and make a statement. I'm not interested in who became ill or what. I can only tell the truth, nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shabani.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome. You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROMANO
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have some questions. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Shabani, you said that some 20 police came to Sadik Osmani's house, they beat and harassed you and ordered you to go towards Bebush Hill. Is it right?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you see at that time any policemen carrying any kind of walkie-talkies or something like that?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, he was speaking somewhere at Sadik Osmani's house. He was speaking to someone. I don't know who it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I notice that you seem to understand some Serbian, Serb language. Do you?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: Yes, I speak a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you remember any conversation which was done through the walkie-talkies at the time?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET SHABANI
utterances.text: No. He was speaking, but I couldn't hear what he was saying and who he was speaking to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Shabani, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You're free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much from the esteemed Tribunal in The Hague. Thank you very much. And I hope that you can carry on fast completing your work here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: A sentiment which should be echoed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And endorsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness -- a few things before he comes in. He was given protective measures and a pseudonym at a time when his desire that his statement shouldn't be made public in advance of giving testimony, perhaps an understandable sentiment, was misunderstood as being concerned about being identified at all. He's actually happy to give evidence completely openly and will do so. He's the KLA commander in Racak at the material time, and it may be helpful before he comes in if I -- I don't know if the Chamber is using the road map that we've been providing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In which case, in addition to the -- I can't find it. I've marked certain places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In addition to the town of Racak -- the village of Racak itself, places to which he will refer include: To the west of Racak there's Rance, almost at the same level; south of Racak there's Petrova; and then south-east of that there's Mullopolc. On the square to the left of Racak, there's a gorge which is referred to. I can hardly read it now myself, spectacles not sufficient, but it's Laniste. And those are various places that will be referred to. Your Honour, although he of course can provide evidence about the KLA, and I'll get him to give some, it's quite important, in our submission, that the evidence is properly confined because this is not a case about what the KLA is doing. It's about other things. So although his statement contains a great deal of detail, I'm not going to go into that, and I hope to confine his evidence to what is material to this trial. One last thing: Several witnesses now have spoken of mutilation of bodies at Racak, hearts being cut out and so on. It may be, and this will be an argument in due course, and may be that that is explicable by damage done to bodies by gunshot and similar weaponry. It's rather distressing to show such photographs either at all, given that there's a public viewing, but also to witnesses who were there at the time and don't necessarily need to have these memories revived. With this witness, it is necessary to look at the bodies in the ravine, and although not an attractive exercise, we will, in the course of that, be looking at one such body, the chest of whom has been so destroyed, apparently by gunshot or by some other similar weapon as perhaps to give the impression of mutilation where there in fact may have been no mutilation other than that that caused his death. So if I linger on that to a limited extent with this witness, it's to deal with that comment or possible comment in due course and to save other witnesses from having to relive their experiences. We'll also ask for a blackboard to be brought in and the large plans, and then may the witness come in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your full name, please.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: My name is Shukri Buja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, is it right that in 1999, you were the KLA commander in Racak?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I was commander of the Nerodime Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which included Racak?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that shortly, but let's first hear a little of your personal history. You're presently 36 years old?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apparently self-employed, with your own business.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1989, were you involved in demonstrations in Kosovo about the political situation?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they initially peaceful or violent demonstrations?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: They were peaceful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could move a little closer towards the microphone then you'll be heard that much more easily. Thank you so much. Did the police intervene in the demonstrations?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. They intervened with violence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you, in due course, arrested?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. I was arrested on the 7th of June, 1989.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that we can have an idea of what it was like to be arrested for taking part in a demonstration at that time, how were you treated at the investigation, the interrogation stage?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The interrogation lasted for three months, and there was a lot of violence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the violence on you such as to leave marks that you were able to show to other people?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. I did show them to the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to the court hearing in a second, but before that, who did you understand to be the prosecutor of your case at that hearing?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I think it was Danica Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That same name as the name of the woman judge who came to Racak to conduct the investigation there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I think so. I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You showed your marks to the court. How long did your trial last for this political offence?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: About three hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the sentence?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I was given a 13-year gaol sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that sentence, in your experience, in line with or greater than or less than sentences being imposed at that time for similar activity?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: At that time, all political activists were given 15, ten, or less years to serve in gaol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In gaol, as a political prisoner, were you dealt with separately from other prisoners - robbers, thieves, rapists, or whatever - or were you dealt with in the same prison system?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We were kept in the same place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you subject to any maltreatment by the authorities while in prison or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Yes" meaning there was maltreatment?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your 13-year sentence, did you serve five years, being released in 1994?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the police when you were released? Did they leave you alone or did they keep in contact with you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The first and the very first day before reaching the house, they stopped and kept me for two hours in the street and threatened that if people were to turn out to welcome me on my way home, they'd re-arrest me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yield to those indications by the police? Did you give into them or did you maintain your independence?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I maintained my independence because I was -- neither was I able to organise people to come -- to come out and welcome me, and neither was I able to turn them away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the police try and keep in contact with you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The police came and re-arrested me. They questioned me for two days on end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we move on, you were one of a number of people detained for taking part in demonstrations with these prison sentences. Just to your knowledge - yes or no - did the accused ever say anything publicly about such demonstrators?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. He usually called them separatist-terrorist demonstrations. Or phraseology of this kind was used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what media are you referring to; television, radio, newspapers, or what?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: They were public statements on television, the radio, the print media, the daily print media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You left Kosovo in what year initially?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I left Kosova in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going to live where?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I sought political asylum in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you live there for some time, pursuing when there the interests of Kosovo Albanians?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. I lived there, and I was involved in activities that had helped my own compatriots in Kosova, and we organised rallies, various kinds of rallies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Peaceful rallies in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any trouble or did you get into any trouble with the Swiss authorities?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you for a time pursue the occupation of journalist?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Switzerland or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Mainly in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, just to go back, at the time when he was arrested in 1989, I'd just like to find out what occupation was he involved in. When you were arrested in 1989, what work were you doing at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was a student in Prishtina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You were a student. I see, yes. And when did you get married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1987.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you were married at the time when you were arrested. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far as you are concerned, when did the KLA first come into being?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, the KLA became known to me in 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first support it?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The beginning of the year of 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that stage, were its intentions militaristic so far as you understood them? Were they to deal with the problems they saw by force or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The use of force was the ultimate means to obtain a resolution of the issue of Kosova, and even at that time there was the option that, were it possible to obtain a political solution, the political means ought to be resorted to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that early stage, 1996, were you yourself a military member - you were in Switzerland - or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, because there were no KLA soldiers in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your involvement was purely as what, as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, in giving political support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in due course to return to Kosovo. What was the event that triggered your return?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I returned to Kosova after the Prekaz events where the legendary Commander Adem Jashari and the members of his family and families who lived in the neighbourhood, in the lower Prekaz neighbourhood, were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of that happening, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: As a result of this event, we departed for Albania where we procured light weapons, ammunition, which we had orders to take to Drenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "We" being how many of you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: About 30 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get into Kosovo with your light weaponry?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Armed with our light weapons which over -- for about 70 hours in the hill -- in the mountains of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approaching from where; the north, the south, where?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: From the village of Vlana; that is to say, from the north of Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once back in Kosovo, did you seek any other employment or did you spend your time exclusively for the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I returned in order to work as a journalist for the KLA or within the auspices of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the event, did you work as a journalist or did you take up some other position?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, because the headquarters gave me another task, i.e., organising the units in the municipalities of Shtime, Ferizaj, Kacanik, Malisheva, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was this a military role?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You set out in your statement that's been served, of course, in full on the accused, the amici, and it may even be on the Court, you set out a number of matters about the structure of the KLA, and I'm not going to go into them in any detail. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you used the word "headquarters." Just tell us this: Did the KLA have a formal structure?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, it did have an official structure even though at that period I was not aware of who was a member of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nevertheless, there was a headquarters which issued instructions that you had to follow?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your first task with the new role you'd been given was to do what? Can you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It had to do with recruiting new soldiers, setting up the first units which should operate in the areas that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about weapons? How was the KLA being armed? How was it getting its weapons?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Most of the weapons came from Albania. There were weapons coming from Czechoslovakia, from the Serbian state itself, and weapons -- various weapons from other sources procured in the ways that we were able to do at that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have anything to do with transport of weapons at any time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. I was involved in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you can answer questions of detail if anybody wants to know. Your position as commander of a subzone, I think it is, was from what day or roughly what day?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: From the beginning of 1998, of June 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: June 1998. Thank you. The brigades that fell under your responsibility, what were their numbers?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: In the beginning, it was not a brigade level, but during the first offensive, we were able to get the various units together like the unit Celiku, Sokoli, and other units. Out of them, we were able to put together Brigade Number 121, which became part of the subzone of the -- of Pashtrik, the operational subzone of Pashtrik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is probably more detail than we require, but you can give further detail of that sort if the accused or anybody else wants to know about it.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn now to Racak. Racak fell within your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the two large plans that have been brought in be placed on the easels, please. I gather that the witness has a mobile microphone available to him on the table so that ... May I remind you of the numbers of those exhibits, if Ms. Graham can assist me. It's 94, tab 73 for both maps. These are, of course, much larger versions of them. They're also in the Racak binder. For those viewing from outside the courtroom, we'll see what they're seeing. I don't see anything. The scale of the map on the left is -- I don't know if it's smaller or larger, but it shows the larger area. It shows the general area of Racak set in the municipality of Stimlje. The right-hand of the map shown on the television screens is restricted more to Racak itself. The Chamber has already had evidence from Mr. Kelly about the geography generally, and therefore we can take that as read, although the Chamber may wish to be reminded of the names of the hills. That will come automatically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, can you help us, please, with the construction of bunkers and trenches in and around Racak, when that started and what was the purpose of it all?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And it may be helpful to have the overhead projector ready for use as well and to place on it, for those viewing, the map we have, if somebody can make theirs available. And if we could open it at page 11. Exhibit 33 -- Exhibit 83.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bunkers and the like built in the area of Racak starting when, please, Mr. Buja?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It started in December 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a sentence or so, the significance, the significance to the KLA of Racak as a location.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: For us, the positions above Racak were important to defend the zone of Lluzhak which was important to defend our zone, because this was the only link between the zone of Pashtrik and the General Staff of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters request the witness to draw closer to microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you move more -- could you move closer to the microphone, please, Mr. Buja. The interpreters are having trouble hearing you. Now, if we look at the map on the overhead projector and focus on the Stimlje square which is towards the top and on the right-hand side, and on the square to its left. Going a little further, that would help. Is there a gorge close to Racak that had some bearing on the deployment of forces there? If so, name it and point it out for us.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Important for the KLA forces?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We were positioned on this road, and the bunker was above Recak, here. This position on what we called the Kerkova Road and the Recak bunker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. At the moment, I'm interested in the gorge, and it may be down towards the left-hand side of the screen, towards Laniste. Tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Do you mean the Lluzhak gorge?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The Lluzhak gorge stretches from Petrova. There's a part of the village called Lluzhak, and the gorge goes along here to Lanishte, which was the border with the Pashtrik Operative Zone. And that was our link with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how important was this route through this gorge to the neighbouring zone and the General Staff? How important was it?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It was important because we kept continual contact with the General Staff, and then had links with Pashtrik operational zone so we could coordinate operations when necessary, and supplies and logistics operated along this route, and the whole life of our operational zone depended on this road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. Now looking at the right hand of the two large maps on the easels, and using the portable microphone that's on the desk if you need to, using the left-hand map if it's helpful, or more helpful, can you just show the learned Judges where the bunker was that you created in December of 1998.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The bunker was in this position here. Here were the channels that connected the bunkers with the base. Here was the bunker of the KLA. And this bunker was in a position which connected it with our positions on the Kerkova Road. Above the Kerkova Road, there is a range of mountains which is known as the gorge of Lluzhak, here, in this part down here, which you can't actually see on this map. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. By the time of the major incident in Racak in January, had any other trenches or fortifications been started to be built?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, work had started, but it had not been completed. In this direction, from this area, approximately, this is where the KLA defence trenches were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were they in use by the time of the Racak incident?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's now turn to the village itself, and using that same right-hand large map, did the KLA have a presence in the village; and if so, can you show us on the map whereabouts it was that they had that presence.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The KLA was positioned in this gorge, and from here there was a KLA guard which didn't allow civilians to go in. And this area was the KLA unit's base.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The witness has marked the area of buildings and houses generally to the right of the figure "2" on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it one building or more than one building that the KLA had occupation of?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There were several buildings, about five or six houses, that were used for accommodation, catering for the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the KLA were there - and we'll see when they were there, but in 1999 certainly - were non-KLA villagers allowed there or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No interpretation.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: As soon as -- the civilians were not allowed in this area, because as soon as villagers of Recak left their village and went to Shtime, they were maltreated by the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were maltreated by the police. Is this in connection with their having left because of the KLA, or is this because of their connection with the KLA? Why do you tell us about their maltreatment by the police?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: This is about the villagers of Recak who lived in Recak, and when they went to Shtime to go shopping and didn't have any connection with the KLA, they were still maltreated by the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how does that lead to them being excluded from the areas of the village occupied by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We know that the first offensive was in August 1998, and in this offensive a lot of civilians of Recak left because their houses were burned, and there were very few inhabitants. So some houses were given over to us voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you speak of the first offensive in August 1998 in Racak. Were you there yourself at the time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I was present, but not in the territory. We didn't have soldiers in this territory, because in Recak, Petrova, Mullopolc, there were no KLA units. The only KLA was in the village of Rance and in Jezerc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... already to the west. So you learnt of the first offensive by what you were told by others; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but also from the smoke and the flames rising from the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it following that that the KLA made its presence, built the bunkers and the trenches?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. This was in August 1998 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: -- when we didn't have any positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was only after that that you did make positions?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The January 1999 incident, the attack, what, as far as you could judge at the time, triggered it? What caused it?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The reason was the policy of ethnic cleansing. But on the basis of analysis done on a preliminary basis, it was the result of an operation that was planned, with the positioning of Serbian forces at the Shtime pine trees and Pod i Geshtenjeve and the gorge of Caraleva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we come to the positioning of the forces: Was there an event that was, or was used as, a reason for the attack?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. Propaganda from Serbia said that there had been a policeman killed, and one was wounded, and this was an incident provoked by Serbian forces, intended to lead to the arrest of villagers from Slivove.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the map on the overhead projector, we can see Slivovo is in the same square as Racak, but it is -- it's possibly just in sight on the television screen. It's to the right-hand edge of that square, pretty well in the centre of the right-hand margin. And so that would be a distance of some six to eight -- or six kilometres or thereabouts, as the crow flies. Was there any particular connection --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I hope the Chamber can see Slivovo. It's not quite in focus, but it's just underneath and to the left of the number 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any connection, logistical or by reason of inhabitants or anything of that sort, between Slivovo and Racak? Any connection between the two?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There was no connection, but it was a village also with an Albanian population. And the Serbian police had been trying to arrest people who fled, and then they were shot at. And a KLA unit came to help the population, and there was a confrontation of about 40 minutes, but we didn't know what casualties were caused, if anybody was killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it forces under your command that had been involved at Slivovo?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It was forces that were positioned on the front line at Mullopolc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these forces the same as or different from the forces that were to be in the area of Racak on about the 14th, 15th of January? Was it the same forces or different forces?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. The Recak unit was another unit, whereas the Mullopolc unit was part of the 1st Battalion of the 161st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Between that incident at Slivovo and the attack in January, had any indication been given publicly that retaliation might occur?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, there had been signs. First was the visit by Vojislav Seselj to Kosova, and he publicly called for vengeance; and then there was the positioning of Serbian forces in the positions I mentioned earlier; and then the operations of paramilitaries known as the Black Hand, who had killed several people in Shtime and Ferizaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Breaking down those three topics: Seselj's visit where he publicly called for vengeance was to which town?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: This was in the same month as the massacre, before the massacre, in 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you remember which town the visit was to and how he made this public call for vengeance? Was it in a speech or in a written communication? What?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: He visited the town of Prishtina and the village of Gracanica and made a speech.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dealing with the Black Hand -- I'm going to ask you some further questions a little later about paramilitaries, but at this stage: The Black Hand was one band of paramilitaries, and you say that there were some killings in the area of Stimlje and Ferizaj between the Slivovo event and the attack on Racak?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There were killings by the Black Hand even before the Slivove incident and also after the NATO bombing, and the Black Hand was in action for a long time. It was not a paramilitary unit in the full sense of the word, but it was under the same command of the politicians in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that later. So there were these killings, and then -- as an indicator, you tell us, of revenge, and then there was the positioning of Serb forces. Before we come to their positioning: Was there, by the beginning of 1999 and the end of 1998, a ceasefire in place pursuant to an agreement that involved Holbrooke and the accused?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, there was the Holbrooke-Milosevic agreement, which was in October, as far as I remember, 1998, when the OSCE observers arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The positioning of Serb forces that you're about to tell us about by using the map in just a minute, would that have been in accord with or in breach of that agreement?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: This was a breach of the agreement, and for that reason the command of the Nerodime operational zone protested to the OSCE about the positioning of the Serb forces, precisely because it was in violation of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now, please, using the pointer, the portable microphone, and the large maps, show us where these forces were deployed; and insofar as you can recall, give us an indication of what forces were deployed.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: May I stand up?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Serbian forces were put here at the place known as Pishat, or pine trees of Shtime. There were armoured vehicles, and we managed to identify 48 armoured vehicles, tanks, Pragas, APCs, and others, and they were also positioned at Pod i Geshtenjeve, where there were also tanks and Pragas. And here they were positioned --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first place you indicated is marked "A" on the map showing the area, the second is at the position marked "C" on that map, and I think you're turning to the area marked "B." Tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Zone C, which is known as Pod i Geshtenjeve, and "A" is here at the pine trees, and they were also positioned at the Caraleva gorge, on the main road to Prizren. These were the positions of Serbian military forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us -- you've given us an idea of the strength of the forces at the position marked "A." Can you give us an idea, please -- and don't guess if you can't recall or didn't discover, but can you give us an idea of the strength of the forces at position "C" and "B"? "C" first.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The ones that I was able to see were tanks and Pragas, and there were also other tanks which we could see at a paper factory that was behind this hill, where there were three tanks positioned. But we weren't able to observe other forces. Those were what we could see here. But here, at "A," by the pine trees, we were able to identify 48 armoured vehicles, and also at the Caraleva gorge. But there were no armoured vehicles, apart from trucks and unarmoured pinzgauers that were by Caraleva where there was a police checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And "B," anything at "B"?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There was no -- at "B," there were no positions before 15th of January, but early in the morning, at about 7.00, there were tanks seen, and Pragas, here. Here, from the position where I was, I was able to see the APC and a Praga, and also one Praga that was hidden behind the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If you'd like to take a seat. You indicated on the map -- and we'll just give the reference points on the map, because people will be reading the transcript later without necessarily having the advantage of the video to hand. You indicated that your position on that morning was at position 10. Can we therefore now turn straight away to that morning. How many KLA altogether were there in this general area of Racak?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There were 47 soldiers in the Racak zone, including the kitchen staff and auxiliaries of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us about the collection of buildings that you occupied, and you've pointed out the bunker and the trenches. Were these 47 soldiers in those two locations or were they in any other parts of the village?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: They were in these two places, and from the base where they slept, they went to the bunkers. And then there were guards at the bunkers, and the bunkers were generally watched. But elsewhere in Recak, there were no soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did the incident start, so far as you were concerned and aware, and at what time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: After the massacre, we analysed the operations of the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd be grateful if, before doing a post-event analysis, you'd just tell the Judges what you were aware of that morning, what you did and what you saw happening to the troops under your command.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: At the start of the attack, and when fire started, I went to my soldiers at the wall, what I call the wall position, and there we joined members of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the wall position, is that the position you've already shown us on the left-hand map, marked 10?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you went there to your soldiers, and you say "when the shooting started." Who started the firing or shooting?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The shooting was begun by the people who started the attack, that is, the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware immediately of where the firing was coming from? You've given three locations where there were forces deployed. Can you tell us where the first shots came from?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The first shots came from "B," from Cesta, towards our positions, and then they continued with artillery support from the pine trees at "A," and also from "C," which was the Geshtenje hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we're coming up to 1.00. Find a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is probably going to be as convenient as any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, you are giving evidence. Would you remember, in this and any other --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're giving evidence. Would you remember, in this and any other adjournments there may be, not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. We'll adjourn now until half past 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'd reached the position of the first shots that you heard fired and you told us where from. What did you do by way of response? What did your soldiers in the village do?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The response of the soldiers was through a short, brief volley from the position of the bunker which also was -- served as a warning to the other soldiers who were at the base. They raised the alarm and started filing out of the base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they successful in getting out of the base, all of them, or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: They started getting out, but some of them came under attack and were killed as they were emerging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many were killed?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There were -- eight were killed during those few moments. Two others were killed while manning the positions at the bunker. It was a soldier called Ismail Luma, who is the commander officer, the commanding soldiers on duty, and another one called Enver Rashiti. So two other soldiers were killed as they were exiting from the house on the stairway, two others at another site belonging to the base as well, another one at a more remote area, where the commander of the unit also sustained injuries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It consisted of 47 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it may be helpful if we just display one other photograph. First of all, before we do, if you look at the right hand of the two maps, the position you've described of the KLA base in the village is on the road leading towards what's marked as number 2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, at this position here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taken from the Racak binder at tab 7 of Volume 1, and the first photograph, there's this photograph. Perhaps you'd be so good as to look at it. Does this show a view looking along the road towards -- we can see crime scene 2 with other locations marked. Does it show the area of buildings that served as the KLA base?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. They were located at that gorge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as we can see from this photograph, they are at an end point of the village. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. They are on the entrance to the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, in a sense, remote from the rest of the village. They can be cut off from the rest of the village.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, because the village is further down whilst the KLA base overlooked it and was isolated and cut off from the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, some ten, I think, men, or thereabouts, were killed at these early stages of the attack. By what time in the morning, approximately, had they died?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: About 7.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Initially, did they stay where they were and where they fell?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. They were left there. It was unable to remove them. The wounded withdrew from the base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the -- the wounded and the unwounded KLA, did they regroup or did they gather together somewhere?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. They regrouped and began their withdrawal, given there were eight wounded amongst our soldiers and it was necessary to take them away. So they withdrew in this direction, in the direction of the gorge of Lluzhak where we regrouped. The commander of the unit was wounded there, Afet Bilalli. And with him was soldier Skender Qarri, who was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you with your men as they withdrew to the gorge?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, because I was manning position number 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stayed in position number 10. Did you fire or return fire to the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. We responded with fire to the forces which emerged at Cesta where the APC and Praga emerged into the open and responded with fire to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What weapons did you have to return fire from your position at position 10, the wall?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: A mortar, calibre 500, and other weapons belonging to the unit of the reconnaissance mission of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the only position from which KLA were firing on the Serbs at that early time of the morning, or were there other positions where the KLA were firing on the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: This was the only position in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in that position, firing on the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Position 10 was the continual position we manned. I did not stay there throughout the day because I had to go and check the front line, which also included the villages of Petrova, Jezerc --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did firing continue from position 10 on --

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: -- and Mullopolc. There was sporadic firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All day?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, all day, from this position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the other men had withdrawn to the gorge. Were they in a position to mount any attack on the Serbs or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The soldiers who withdrew from this unit were mostly incapable of mounting an assault, because part of them, eight of them, had been wounded; eight were initially killed; a tenth one was killed before 11.00; and even their mental state was not one that had lent itself to an assault. So when we started returning the fire in the road towards Kerkova, this was mostly done by soldiers belonging to other units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The road towards Kerkova, can you point that out to us, or to be precise, where it is? Because I don't think it's shown on this map, and we may have to go back to the atlas. The roads towards Kerkova.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It can't be seen on this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'd turn, please, now to the atlas. And so you're speaking of firing by other units on the road to Kerkova. Can you point out what road that is, the road to Kerkova?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: It departed from Petrova, from the Lluzhak gorge, and it continued on the line towards Rance. This road links to the village of Rance. This all followed after 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And fighting on that road, was it the KLA who were on that road, firing on Serb forces elsewhere, or was it the Serb forces who were on that road, according to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: This was a reciprocal firing. Serbian forces were overlooking the village and they were stationed in that part over Recak. And we shot from the Kerkova Road, but we couldn't advance further in order to reposition ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... because remember, you've told us of the existence of Serb forces at the three positions north and east, generally, of Racak. Were people firing from this road to those original positions - A, B, and C - or to another position? Where were the Serbs on whom they were firing?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. From position A, the Pishat, and from Cesta, and from position C, Kodra e Geshtenjeve, the shooting enabled soldiers to be able to -- to regroup or withdraw to those positions like the bunkers. The Serbs were positioned in that part there and another part towards Recak. The other part of the Serbs came from that part over there and from Cesta, where the infantry advanced on the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I follow this correctly - and correct me if I'm wrong - the Serbs, having repositioned themselves south of Racak and in the area where you had previously had fortifications, and north of Racak, were fired upon by the KLA. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. They were positioned in our former positions, basically, and that is the direction we shot towards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The day passes. You've told us about your activity. What happened to the bodies of the soldiers who died early in the morning?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The bodies of the soldiers, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: A soldier who was killed later at the Kodra e Shaqes position, which is further to the south, he was taken away at about 11.00, whilst the soldier -- the commander of the unit, who was injured over there, was able to get through radio link to us and tell us that he had been severely injured. And after dusk fell, we undertook his rescue. We weren't able to do that. We were only able to do that when the Serbian forces apparently began withdrawing. So we returned to our former positions to find dead soldiers, one inside the bunker, another one near the bunker. Then our soldiers started towards the base, where they found soldier Kadri Syla, near the canal which leads towards the bunker, and another soldier killed outside the last house of our base. Two soldiers were found a bit further away, in the other house, and also Skender Qarri, the soldier who was found near the injured commander, Bilalli, and these were taken away. These bodies were taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those bodies were taken away the same night?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... part of your account short, were they in due course buried, I think given a military burial, but were they in due course buried elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Namely, at what village? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: They were buried in the village of Mullopolc --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which the Chamber can see --

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: -- as the commander of the zone decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- on the ELMO, on the overhead projector at the moment, and it's immediately south of Stimlje and some distance away from Racak.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Sorry. The village is immediately south of Stimlje and some way away from Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When locating and retrieving the bodies of the soldiers, Mr. Buja, were any civilians found who had been killed or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: There were civilians who had been killed, but their bodies were not retrieved because the order that we got was to retrieve the bodies of the KLA. There was an order which operated throughout the war that dictated that KLA soldiers ought not to be left at the site where they were killed, but they ought to be retrieved and buried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'd look, please, be good enough to look at the right hand of the two maps in a little -- with a little care, and I want you to help us with two things. First of all, there are a number of locations marked on that map. Starting at number 1 -- forget number 2 for the time being. Starting at number 1 and then going through, if you look at them, 3 to the north, 4 a little to the west of 3, 5 the ravine - and we'll come to the ravine in a minute in more detail - and then 6 up on the hill of Cesta, is it? Did you have any KLA soldiers deployed in any of those positions in the course of this day?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, none at all. Only position number 2 where the KLA base was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the map that's there has on the left-hand side a number of crime location scenes with the names of individuals said to have been killed at those scenes, again omitting the ravine because the number was too large - the names are particularised there - but including names of individuals killed at scene number 2. Have you gone through all those names to see if any of those names are the names of KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen the names. None of the ones that you mentioned were KLA members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first learn that something may have happened in the village to civilians?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: This happened after the civilian population left with some injured in their midst. There was a meeting between the zone commander with the OSCE and the civilians who managed to escape from Recak, and that was where it was learned that a massacre had occurred in Recak, although we treated this very cautiously, as a very suspicious information, because we were receiving a myriad of kinds of information throughout the day. It was the evening of the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at that time able to go and investigate the rumours yourself to see if there was any truth in them or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: On the night of the 15th of January, we were unable to do this because it was winter. There was a lot of snow. It was pitch darkness. And we didn't even venture towards that direction. Instead, we decided to undertake this on the next day when the OSCE verifiers were to go, and Fehmi Mujota was the man in charge of political affairs in the -- in the KLA zonal command was to go with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit the ravine yourself?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The visit -- the visit was by the OSCE team, and within its auspices there was the RS representative, and this happened on the next day, on the 16th of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you visit -- were you one of the people who visited it?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: I went there later, after William Walker had arrived in Recak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask the witness to look at a video of the viewing of the ravine for two purposes. First, for him to tell us one way or another whether any of the people shown dead in the ravine were KLA soldiers; and second, for him to comment on the clothing they're wearing and how that clothing matches, or not, the clothing of the KLA. The video will also serve the purpose that I identified at the beginning of the examination of this witness, the nature of the injuries, stressful though it is. I must make sure I get the right number. I gather it's already with the audio-visual booth as Exhibit 95. Before we start it -- and it's ERN 1599. I'm grateful to Mr. Higgins. And we have some notes of the excerpts for the two videos that we're going to show. And the first excerpt is four minutes and 29 seconds, and the second is two minutes, a little under two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Exhibit 95A, if there's not one already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I believe this is 95. 95A was the extract shown to Lord Ashdown. As this apparently has itself been extracted - Ms. Graham makes sure I'm punctilious - perhaps this should become 95B. Then there'll be -- oh, yes. And I'm reminded that at the end -- we should have sound on with this. At the end, the interview is in Albanian, but it is at a speed that I think can be followed by the interpreters and we would ask them to interpret it for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's the end of that clip. I think there should be another bit to follow, but perhaps we can just break there for a second and ask two questions, if it's not too difficult for the audio-visual booth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the men shown on that footage of video film members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, none of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did the clothing they were wearing compare with the typical clothing at that time of people serving in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: You can't compare, because KLA soldiers had their uniforms --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: -- a different kind of clothing. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other examples, think back, at that time of people wearing clothing like that actually being serving KLA soldiers or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, not in this kind of clothing. We could have had civilian clothing only for the underwear, because we did not have everything to comply with the military uniform in terms of underwear because -- but the outer layer of clothing was always a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we move to the next part of the video, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "I believe you have seen what face the enemy has, the enemy that kidnapped these Albanian civilians and brought them here to be massacred. The -- these images do show the real face of the enemy. And the KLA is always thinking of defending these civilians, protecting them. I can't say any more at this moment. I think this is enough. The message that you're witnessing I think is sufficient. This is not only a Serbian massacre, it is a massacre assisted by the international community. And the Serbian forces -- then Serbian forces, since then, they are positioning in Shtime, Ferizaj, and all the positions forces that they occupied were in breach of the agreement, and when we refrained so as not to break the agreement. And they went behind the back of this village to be able to mount this assault. That's all I have to say."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was, I think, you speaking on the camera, yes?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We saw that you were dressed -- how you were dressed, and that you had two others beside you. Who were the other two beside you or behind you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: They were my officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the clothing that you were wearing typical or unusual for KLA soldiers at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The KLA soldiers wore such uniforms, and there were other kinds of uniforms but they were military ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to deal with a couple of other matters arising from this incident. What level of arms did an individual KLA soldier at the time typically carry? How many weapons?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: KLA soldiers were armed with automatic weapons, and some of them had 47s. There were soldiers without automatic weapons, but they had 12.7s, 7.9s, and there were auxiliaries with 12.7s and 7.9, and maybe they had the occasional revolver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any individual soldier typically have more than one firearm at any given time or not?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We didn't even have enough to arm -- give one to each soldier let alone let any soldier have two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which brings me to this issue: You lost some ten soldiers in the early stages, and you'd lost possession of the base down there in the village; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes. We had lost eight soldiers at the start of the fighting and then another one on the hill at about 11.00. And there were eight soldiers also wounded in various degrees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us with how many weapons altogether you lost or may have lost, as a result of this incident, to the Serb forces or to other forces that entered the village?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: We lost four automatic rifles and also some 12.7s and one 7.9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many 7.9s did you have altogether?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: One, and one 12.7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware at the time - I think you've already perhaps told us this - of an investigation conducted or sought to be conducted in Racak by a judge?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Excuse me. When? When do you mean this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the attack and after the visit by the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, indeed, who you understood the name of the judge to be. You've told us about the loss of weapons from individual soldiers, as it were, the maximum that could have been lost. What about from the base itself, the buildings? Was there any cache or store of weapons there that could have been taken by the judge conducting this investigation, or those acting on her behalf?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: They might have taken four automatic weapons from the killed soldiers, they might have taken two bandoliers with bullets, which our soldiers had, and a quantity of automatic rifle munition.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask the witness now to look at another video, which is, as I explained yesterday, a video very recently provided by the Serbian authorities as part of the Marinkovic inquiry. It's V0003923, and will therefore require an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 210.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And if the video booth could be good enough to play that video. I would ask you, Mr. Buja, to look at it so as in due course to comment on whether any part of this could be -- or whether all of it could be weaponry taken from the KLA at Racak at this time. It may be helpful if during this first 17 seconds we pause it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as to what you've just been looking at there, what do you say as to the possibility of that being weaponry taken from KLA soldiers: possible or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: They resembled our weapons, especially the heavy one, the 12.7, and the automatic weapons, but not the big great chest that is there and the other quantities of munitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Press on, then, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think it goes on a little, if we can, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You can fast-forward to the end of this clip, please. Pausing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The weapons you've just been looking at, what do you say to the possibility -- we haven't yet had the report to translate it from the Serbian, it only having arrived a couple of days ago, but what do you say as to the possibility of those weapons being KLA weapons, and what do you say about their condition of cleanliness and newness?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: The quantity of weapons here is very large, and we didn't have this quantity, even if two units had joined the Recak and Rance units. This is a very large quantity, and it's known very well that our base in Recak, there were -- nine soldiers were killed. There's far too many weapons here for nine soldiers. There was one 12.7 and one 7.9 was taken. And the quantity shown here is far too large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of the weapons?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: First of all, the KLA soldiers didn't have automatic rifles with bayonets. They all bore without bayonets. And also the number of hand grenades here was not even in the hands of even the special units that were under the command of the zone commander. Not even they had so many grenades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not going to deal with the rest of this video. We can see that there is another extract, number 4, with grenades and bullets, but I don't propose to take time exploring it. It's there for the accused, if he wants to ask any questions about it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few other questions of a general nature, but before we come to them: The village of Racak, you had had some concerns from the deployment of Serb troops and from other events that an attack was likely. Was any advice given to the villagers?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Generally, our soldiers, and the sector for relations with civilians, maintained discussions with villagers in cases of danger, just as it did in 1998, when, from Rance, we warned the civilians about the danger of the Serbian offensive, and also warned before the fighting started in Recak. We never gave them orders to go, but they themselves, the majority of the inhabitants of Recak, decided to stay in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two other documents I'd like you to look at briefly, already produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Exhibit 179, please. Your Honour, this is a document already produced by General Maisonneuve, recording a conversation or meeting he had with Colonel Bogoljub Janicijevic on the 16th of January. And if the English could be laid on the ELMO, the overhead projector, and the original given to the witness, who I think reads --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The B/C/S copy for the witness. And if we look at it on the overhead projector to see what passages I'm asking his comment on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the centre of the screen, there's a passage which reads as follows, and I'd like your comment on it for its accuracy, but I'll read it out in English: [As read] "Suspect 15 terrorists killed. Tried to find them. No one in village. Went to forest and bunkers little bit up from village. Believe their central headquarters in Luzhnice, where a large group opened fire with a 12.7 gun. KLA used snipers, Chinese MGs, fired mines toward police and Chinese 81-millimetre mortar over the hill. Police searched until reaching bunkers, stopping because of fire, but after forcing personnel out of bunkers whom ran over hill, finding wpns (1 Browning, 2 HMG 12.7, few mines for hand launcher, 36 automatic rifles, 2.000 rounds, 2 sniper rifles, and other inf supplies)." What do you say as to the accuracy of that account?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, they're not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you were having some trouble with the translation. What do you say to the accuracy of any part of it? Were there 15 terrorists killed? Mr. Buja, are you hearing me?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a case of there being 15 terrorists killed, or less, assuming that "terrorists" means KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: First, I don't know which HQ is mentioned here in Luzhnice. I have a document in front of me in Serbo-Croatian, and it says "Luzhnice" which was not in my zone of responsibility and is a very long way from Recak. And I can't answer as to whether they captured any kinds of weapons. But the unit of Recak and its base, there were four automatic rifles taken, one 12.7, and one 7.9, as I said before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that if at Luzhnice, which we can find on our map at page 11, P19, I think -- yes, it's right at the top and is clearly some over 10 kilometres away. If they found any of these things, did that have anything to do with KLA activity in Racak?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No, because we didn't have units of our zones or any -- any units of our zone or units connected with our zone in Luzhnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If the usher would be good enough to turn us to the second sheet in the English, and in the middle of the page there's a reference there to -- pretty well in the middle of the screen: "At the beginning of the OP saw men in black uniforms, UCK policemen, using women and children as a shield." Two points -- three points: Did the KLA or UCK have some troops that wore black uniforms? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any UCK troops in black uniforms deployed in Racak on this day?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: No. Not at Recak, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any question of UCK using women and children as shields at Racak on this day or ever? But Racak on this day is all that we're really concerned with.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA
utterances.text: Of course not, because this was the Albanian population, and these were our families and cousins, the relatives of the soldiers themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
